title: Signal steward cadence and trace contracts — scrapbook
content:
Purpose
This is an informal 'scrapbook' capturing a proposed operational cadence and a compact trace/metric contract for model and routing rollouts. Goal: give teams a lightweight, repeatable checklist to verify observability health during short-lived experiments and longer rollouts. It intentionally prioritizes speed-to-diagnosis and low signal overhead.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to inference surface: hosted API, dedicated pools, private deployments.
- Focus on token-serving latency, KV/prefix cache signals, model-fallback behavior, and UI-visible error rates.
- Not a full instrumentation spec — this complements the instrumentation repo and the canonical metric-contracts doc.

High-level cadence (operational rhythm)
- Weekly: signal steward sync (30m) — owners review flagged signals, anomalies from the past 7 days, and any Dashboard changes in staging.
- Pre-rollout (canary): preflight checklist run with an engineer + steward (15–30m).
- Rollout day: staggered checks at T+5m, T+30m, T+2h, T+24h for canaries; automated probes run every 1m.
- Monthly: signal retirement review and panel pruning (30–60m).

Core metric set (compact, with suggested evaluation queries)
- model_p95_inference_latency_ms
  - intent: measure 95th percentile server-side inference latency (end-to-end token emit path)
  - query sketch: p95(latency_ms){route:model/*,region,tenant} over 5m windows
  - alert heuristics: > baseline + 35% sustained for 10m or absolute > 1.2s

- kv_cache_hit_rate
  - intent: fraction of requests served from prefix/KV cache vs cold path
  - query sketch: sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_lookups) by (model_variant,region) 5m
  - alert heuristics: drop >20% vs rolling baseline for 15m (indicates eviction, config change)

- prefix_warm_start_time_ms
  - intent: time to first-token when client KV/prefix must be reconstructed (measures cold-start pain)
  - query: avg(first_token_latency) filtered by session_is_cold=true
  - use: driving canary decisions for prefetch policies

- server_error_rate (5m)
  - intent: op-level errors (500-series, model failures), exclude client aborts
  - query: count(status>=500)/count(total_requests) by (model,route)
  - alert heuristics: >0.5% sustained or step-change 5x baseline

- user_perceived_ttfb_ms (client-side probe)
  - intent: synthetic probe for time-to-first-byte from representative regions/tenants
  - use: sanity on routing & network problems

Trace annotation / span contract (compact)
- span naming conventions
  - inference.request — parent span for request surface (gateway edge -> router)
  - model.exec — internal spans representing model forward pass(s) and kernel execution
  - kv.lookup — spans for any KV/cache query flow, include size/eviction tags
  - fallback.route — span created when request is routed to fallback variant/region

- required attributes (attached to inference.request or model.exec as appropriate)
  - request_id (string)
  - tenant_id (string)
  - model_name (string) e.g., 'redwood-v1-13b'
  - model_variant (string)
  - region (string)
  - seq_len (int)
  - kv_cache_hit (bool) when relevant
  - fallback_reason (string) when fallback.route spans appear

- sampling guidance
  - Baseline: adaptive sampling — keep 100% of error spans (status>=500 or fallback_reason set), and target 1% of success traces globally with proportional representation across models and regions.
  - For high-volume routes (>=100k qps), apply deterministic reservoir sampling keyed on tenant_id to ensure long-tail tenants retain representation.

Dashboard & probe checklist (preflight and ongoing)
- Preflight (before canary / model swap):
  1) Confirm synthetic probes green for user_perceived_ttfb and example prompts (T-30m).
  2) Baseline p95 inferred and kv_cache_hit_rate snapshot recorded (T-20m).
  3) Ensure alert routes have current owners and runbook links (T-15m).
  4) Start canary at low traffic and monitor T+5m p95 and server_error_rate for step changes.

- Rolling monitoring windows and dashboards
  - Mini-dashboard (canary view): p95, p50, kv_cache_hit_rate, server_error_rate, prefix_warm_start_time, fallback counts, active model_variant distribution. 1m refresh for first hour, 5m thereafter.
  - Operator view (compact): aggregated by tenant weight, includes top-5 tenants contributing to p95 and alerting traces.

Signal retirement decision table (quick heuristics)
- Candidate signal must show one of: low diagnostic value, high query cost, duplication of another signal.
- Retirement checklist:
  - Has not fired for production incidents in 6 months? (yes/no)
  - Is there a downstream dashboard or alert depending on it? (list owners)
  - Can it be approximated by cheaper aggregate? (yes/no)
  - If retire -> annotate deprecation date, owners notified, keep archived query for 90 days.

Runbook snippet: cold-cache spike investigation (common case)
1) Check kv_cache_hit_rate by model_variant and region for a sudden drop.
2) Inspect prefix_warm_start_time distribution and the number of distinct sessions marked cold.
3) Pull traces where kv.lookup spans show long latencies; examine eviction tags and memory pressure signals.
4) Validate recent deploys / kernel changes / quantization toggles for variants in the timespan.
5) If fallback counts rose concurrently, correlate with fallback_reason tag and region routing changes.

Experiment telemetry tagging (lightweight)
- All experiment traffic must include: experiment_id, experiment_arm, sampling_seed (for reproducible trace sampling).
- Tagging must be present in both metrics (as labels) and traces (as attributes) for quick crosswalk in debug workflows.

Operator ergonomics and low-friction defaults
- Panels should default to a 24h focus with quick toggles for 1h/6h/7d.
- Compact alert messages: include top 3 contextual anchors: model_variant, region, top-tenant-by-weight.
- For high-noise signals, quarantine alerts behind 'investigate' label for 48h before promoting to primary page.

Open questions and follow-ups (for next steward sync)
- What exact bounded cardinality value do we want for tenant tagging on p95 panels to keep query cost predictable? (proposal: top-10 tenants + an other bucket)
- How aggressive should adaptive trace sampling be for long-running sessions? (optimize for representative tail vs cost)
- Should we persist a short-lived index of 'recently-changed-models' to speed root cause mapping on deploy days?

Appendix: quick SQL/PromQL sketches and links
- p95 latency (PromQL-like): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_variant))
- kv hit rate: sum(rate(kv_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_lookup_total[5m]))
- example trace filter to find fallbacks: traces where fallback_reason != "" and kv_cache_hit == false

Notes on adoption
This is intentionally compact: teams should copy the sections that match their workflow, and iterate. The goal is to reduce time-to-signal and make canary decisions reproducible. Next steps: land a lightweight steward rota, pilot the canary mini-dashboard for two upcoming rollouts, and collect feedback on trace-sampling knobs.
